# ZBoard v0.0.2

This stable release includes the v0.0.2 RC changes and the latest offline kernel installation and task-retry fixes. ZBoard remains a minimal, extensible panel for users, subscriptions, nodes and system services.

## Highlights

- Refresh the administration interface with shared controls, contextual links, server-side search and paging, compact task views and independently loaded dashboard reports. Preserve existing menu customizations, plugin attachments and optional integrations.
- Correct subscription purchases, plan changes, renewals, paid traffic resets and expiry cleanup. Purchase actions come from published products and saleable SKUs; archived products preserve historical orders. Exhausted renewable subscriptions remain recoverable within the documented grace period.
- Preserve authorized node routes across panel interruptions and avoid restarting Zero when the effective configuration is unchanged. Configuration publication remains a task result; node usability requires activation and health checks.
- Add external forwarding entries without requiring a panel-managed forwarding server. Direct and forwarding access remain independently authorized, with parent credentials reconciled when membership changes.
- Add timezone-aware revenue comparisons, bounded traffic trends and node/user rankings, transactional hourly traffic aggregates, and audited protocol traffic display-baseline resets. Display-baseline resets do not erase the usage ledger or subscription accounting.
- Reduce Connector receipt lock contention with durable spool acceptance, coalesced node receipts, bounded MySQL transactions and repeat-safe accounting. Preserve credential checks, rollback and replay behavior.
- Add administrator-controlled subscription email alerts for low traffic, exhaustion, approaching expiry and expiry. Each alert type defaults to disabled. Administrators configure thresholds and a shared per-user frequency limit; durable deduplication and delivery-time eligibility checks prevent obsolete or repeated reminders.
- Install locally uploaded Zero kernels on Linux x86_64 systemd nodes over authenticated SCP, using the existing verified SSH host identity. Accept raw ELF or official tar.gz packages up to 128 MiB. Validate the artifact, verify the remote SHA and actual build version, and reuse installation health checks and rollback. The panel retains uploaded artifacts in a bounded, persistent store; installation does not fetch the kernel artifact from GitHub.
- Recover duplicate asynchronous task submissions idempotently: an identical retry returns the original task, while a reused key with different content is rejected.

## Downloads

- Docker image: `ghcr.io/zerodenet/zboard:v0.0.2` (also published as `latest`).
- Linux amd64 backend: `zboard_v0.0.2_linux_amd64.tar.gz`, including the offline node cleanup script.
- Offline Docker image: `zboard_v0.0.2_linux_amd64-image.tar.gz`, including the web console.
- `SHA256SUMS` verifies both archives.

The binary package serves an externally supplied web directory; the Docker image includes the web console. Zero node protocol availability depends on the installed kernel build and successful configuration validation, activation and health checks.

## Upgrading

Back up the database, deployment configuration, credential encryption key, plugin packages and managed rules. Preserve the previous image and a pre-upgrade database snapshot for rollback. Prefer the explicit `v0.0.2` image tag for repeatable deployments.

An upgrade from v0.0.1 applies migrations 0022 through 0029: catalog archiving, subscription lifecycle, hourly traffic aggregates, application-owned MySQL hourly writes, fixed-quota lifecycle, external forwarding entries, protocol display-baseline resets and durable subscription alert deduplication. Existing RC installations apply only migrations not already recorded.

For MySQL, stop other application writers and run one instance with `-migrate-only`, then start the application after migration completes. Do not race DDL between instances or run old and new writers together. Migration 0024 repairs partial installations and backfills aggregates from the original ledger; do not delete that ledger, mark a failed migration complete manually or enable global function trust. Migration 0025 removes the old MySQL triggers using the usual schema-level TRIGGER permission; SUPER is not required. SQLite retains its transaction-local triggers. Rolling back to a binary that expects the old triggers requires the pre-upgrade database snapshot as well as the previous binary. Preserve that snapshot when rolling back external forwarding support too.

Use the updated Compose configuration so `/var/lib/zboard/artifacts/kernel-uploads` has its separate writable, persistent mount under the otherwise read-only artifact root. Custom reverse proxies must allow the node kernel upload route's request size and timeout; the included Nginx configuration uses a 129 MiB request limit for that route.

Subscription emails require working SMTP settings and explicitly enabled alert switches. Paid customer traffic resets require a published reset SKU; automatic reset schedules and administrator quota changes remain separate operations.

## Validation

The integrated develop commit passed all six CI jobs: backend, actual MySQL migration/transaction tests, frontend, ZRS compiler, Compose and OpenAPI. Local backend tests/vet, frontend CI-scope tests and production build also passed, including a real SCP sink integration test. Six pre-existing frontend source-policy test files remain excluded from CI under issue #57.

Release CI rebuilds the Linux binary and Docker image. Publication does not deploy an installation, migrate a production database, prove SMTP delivery or complete a production-node offline installation; those checks remain deployment acceptance tasks.
